headline: Claude puts tables and dashboards right into chat, and office folks win
summary: Claude rolls out whiteboards, tables, and data analysis, while Gemini 4 Carbon opens to everyone; both are worth trying today.

items.title: Claude moves whiteboards, tables, and data analysis into the chat
items.pitch: Claude can now open a whiteboard, edit tables, and turn metrics into dashboards and narrated videos right in the conversation—your comp report is saved.
why: Edit tables and whiteboards right in the chat, no more exporting and re-importing
Claude Data turns metrics into dashboards and videos with voiceover
Open Adobe, Atlassian, and Box full-screen through connectors and edit directly
actions: Find the Sheets and Data entry points on Claude web or desktop (paid tiers start rolling out today)
Check the official notes to see how the new whiteboard, tables, and data analysis work
deep_dive: Different from what you do now: before, getting Claude to work on a table meant exporting and re-importing; now it edits as you chat, and Whiteboard is good for sketching the structure first, then filling in the numbers.

Data (formerly Dashboards) is clearly built for non-technical people: drop in a set of metrics, and it builds a shareable dashboard, a data story, even a narrated video—that saves a lot of work on quarterly comp reviews.
Easy to try, and paid tiers are already rolling out. Downside: new features ship in batches, so you might get tables today and the rest tomorrow.
items.signals: HN 243 points · 173 comments · official rollout today · Box CEO backs MCP read/write

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is open to everyone
items.pitch: Gemini 4 Carbon used to be only for safety folks, and today it's available to all; both Simon Willison and Dan Shipper say it's clearly better at coding.
why: Codes better than Argon, and Dan Shipper says in real tests it can go for hours
Global Ultra access in the Gemini App, and /swarm in Antigravity
$2/$10 per million tokens now, doubles Dec 1, so try it early
actions: Switch to Gemini 4 Carbon in the Gemini App (Ultra subscription), or try /swarm in Google Antigravity
deep_dive: Different from the Claude Code/Codex you use: Carbon is Gemini's new flagship, reached through the Gemini App and Antigravity IDE; /swarm splits work across sub-agents, and in Sundar's demo it modeled, wrote a game, and did voiceover on its own.
Easy to get started, and Ultra can use it directly. Downside: Dan Shipper says on long tasks it often "doesn't know when to stop," and Simon's max tier burned through tokens without delivering.
items.signals: Simon Willison tested it · Dan Shipper's same-day vibe check · global Ultra access · price doubles 12/1

items.title: Stop agents from writing 2019 JavaScript
items.pitch: The Chrome team packaged a set of modern web rules; paste them into your coding agent and it'll write less old-school JS and produce cleaner pages.
why: Specifically fixes the agent habit of copying old code and writing old-style JavaScript
Made by Paul Irish, set it up once and Claude Code/Codex both benefit
actions: Go to github.com/googlechrome, find this Show HN project, and add it to your agent config as instructed
deep_dive: Doesn't change which tool you use: it just feeds Claude Code/Codex a "modern web practices" reference so they stop generating old-style code.
Very low cost, just drop it into project rules or a skill. Limit: it only covers frontend web work, not plain scripts or spreadsheet tasks.
items.signals: HN 386 points · 121 comments · released by Google Chrome team / Paul Irish

still_tracking.name: Claude Fable 5.2
still_tracking.update: Simon Willison found a prompt trick: after writing "the codebase is yours," the chance it agrees to merge duplicate code jumped from under 10% to about half; but the max tier burns through tokens and fails to deliver the diagram.
